title: cli/validate: an objectExtensions entry that re-declares an owner's field in `fields` is not refused, though ADR-0146 D10 refuses it on the extension (the registry only warns)
body:
domain:spec#3 · os-sales · session_01L6bhgTqqeHSwZYJmApbDCa

Filing gate: ① a gap between a ratified rule and its doors, found by the contract review of PR #30533 (comment 6665186290, ③ "Added by this review", escalated to the seat for a card). ⛔ Not a claim.

**Business reason.** ADR-0146 D10 (`docs/adr/0146-…` :510-517): "A base field is changed only within a display-property whitelist … Everything else on a base field — type, `required`, `unique`, `reference`, `defaultValue`, formulas, `options` membership — is refused on the extension with a prescription naming the whitelist." An extension that writes an owner's field into its `fields` map instead of `fieldPatches` replaces the owner's definition whole: `packages/objectql/src/registry.ts#mergeObjectDefinitions` (:876-889, `{ ...base.fields, ...extension.fields }`). Nothing refuses that on entry, so a module package can silently turn an owner's writable `amount: number` into `text`, `readonly: true` or a `formula`, and every reader (the engine, and since PR #30533 the lint rules) then judges the field on the extension's definition.

## What the code says (at `origin/main` `4831d500`)

- `packages/objectql/src/registry.ts#reportRedeclaredFields` (:5076): when an owner and an extension (or two extensions) declare the same name in `fields`, the registry `console.warn`s which definition is served. Its docblock: "⛔ Never a refusal, and the served definition is unchanged" (the fold runs on every read while a boot is still registering packages, so the registry is the wrong door to refuse at).
- `packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-extension-field-suffix.ts` (`judgeExtensionFieldSuffix`): the only mechanical extension judge at publish, `os validate` and the install door; it judges the `__c` suffix (reserved to `.custom`; unsuffixed keys inside a `.custom` pair), not a plain-spelled re-declaration of an owner field by a vendor module (ADR-0029 D7 / ADR-0141 D7 keep that spelling plain).
- PR #30533's review, ①.3: the shape reaches `os validate` today, and after #30533 the type, readonly and sort rules judge it on the extension's definition (declared in that PR as part of its narrowing).

## Wanted

- A door that refuses, at `os validate` and at publish (and the install door, the three points D10 names for `__c`), an `objectExtensions[].fields` key naming a field the extended object's owner declares, with a prescription naming `fieldPatches` and the display-property whitelist, when the entry changes anything outside that whitelist. Where the door lives (the authoring gate beside `judgeExtensionFieldSuffix`, or a lint rule run by `os validate`) is the implementing card's measurement.
- Measure first: how many first-party artifacts (examples, HotCRM) re-declare an owner field today; a refusal of shapes in use is a `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` with its ADR-0087 disposition.
- The registry warning stays (it serves bodies no door judged).

Dedupe: `repo:objectstack-ai/objectstack is:issue is:open fieldPatches` → 7 hits; #28804 (skills evals: no eval checks that an author patches with `fieldPatches` instead of taking a field over in `fields`) is the authoring-guidance half of the same rule, not a door; the rest are QA run cards and seat posts. `"D10" extension base field refused` → seat posts and QA runs only. **New.**

Suggested-grade: p2 · a ratified ADR rule with no refusing door; a vendor module can change an owner field's type or writability silently.
